title: Closed models [notes postérieures à PS ?] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: notes on closed model categories (Quillen), apparently written after Pursuing Stacks. The cylinder is written X⊗I, the interval being the 'J' in the handwriting. This is subsection (e) of an argument whose setting is the commutative square g: X→Y, g': X'→Y', i: X→X', p: Y→Y', where i is a cofibration and p is a fibration. A diagonal φ = θ0: X'→Y is given that solves the lifting problem only up to homotopy: φi ≃ g and pφ ≃ g'. A second diagonal θ1 = φ̄ is the wanted strict lift. The previous page has the standard lifting square A→X, A×I→Y with a cofibration and a fibration, plus its dual with A^I.

Top of page. By assumption there are homotopies h: X⊗I→Y from g0 = φi to g1 = g, and h': X'⊗I→Y' from g'0 = pφ to g'1 = g'. 'All we have to do is to check that we can choose these homotopies compatible with i and p', that is, with p∘h = h'∘(i⊗I). Given such a compatible pair, the standard argument yields a strict lift:
- extend h along the cofibration i (relative homotopy lifting against p, with h' as the target homotopy);
- transport φ to a diagonal φ̄ with φ̄i = g and pφ̄ = g'.
This is the classical principle 'a lift up to coherent homotopy implies a strict lift' for cofibration/fibration pairs.

Grothendieck first tries to package the data as a single lifting problem: (X⊔X)⊔(X'⊔X') → X⊗I ⊔ X'⊗I → ... (crossed out). He then observes that the prism with faces h, h', i⊗I, p is not commutative. It commutes only after restricting along the end inclusion X⊔X → X⊗I, because both p∘h and h'∘(i⊗I) have ends pφi = g'0 i and pg = g'i.

Reformulation: set u = (g0, g1): X⊔X → Y and v = h'(i⊗I): X⊗I → Y'. This gives a square with j: X⊔X → X⊗I and p a fibration, and one seeks k (the corrected h) with kj = u and pk = v. The original h gives kj = u, but only pk ≃ v (presumably rel X⊔X, the superscript 's'). Since j is merely a cofibration, not a trivial one, no lift is automatic. The obstruction is precisely a 2-dimensional homotopy, i.e. a coherence between the two homotopies. Remark: if Y' is the final object, p∘h = h'(i⊗I) holds trivially and one is done.

The whole lower half, and this approach, is struck through. The next page restarts with relabelled data (k, h, g0 = φ, g1 = g, g'0 = pψ).
errors: The prism p∘h = h'∘(i⊗I) does not commute in general. Grothendieck notices this himself; this is why the approach is struck out. Arbitrary homotopies cannot simply be 'chosen compatible' without an extra coherence (a homotopy between the homotopies, rel ends) or a modification step.

If the left-margin label on j: X⊔X→X⊗I is read as 'trivial cofibration', it would be wrong: the end inclusion of a cylinder is a cofibration but not a weak equivalence. The handwriting likely reads 'non trivial cofibration', which is consistent with the remark that only pk ≃ v is obtained.

The hypothesis φi ≃ g, pφ ≃ g' (separate homotopies) is insufficient in general for a strict lift. One needs a compatible pair, or must exploit freedom in choosing φ. This gap is exactly what the page is probing and does not close.

ideas.what: A diagonal filler up to homotopy, with homotopies compatible along i and p, can be rectified to a strict filler when i is a cofibration and p a fibration.
ideas.modern_name: Homotopy lifting / rectification of homotopy-commutative lifts; relative homotopy extension (covering homotopy extension)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Strøm 1966-72 for spaces; Quillen 1967 Homotopical Algebra; standard in Hovey/Hirschhorn)
ideas.where_published: Pursuing Stacks discusses cylinders, homotopy intervals and modelizers, but this specific lemma there is unsure

ideas.what: Recasting compatibility of homotopies as a relative lifting problem for (X⊔X → X⊗I) against p, with obstruction a homotopy rel ends.
ideas.modern_name: Relative lifting against the boundary inclusion of a cylinder; 2-cells / homotopies of homotopies
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard homotopical algebra (Quillen; Kamps–Porter abstract homotopy theory)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine scratch work on a standard lemma of model-category theory. Grothendieck finds the coherence obstruction (the prism commutes only on the ends) and abandons the approach. Nothing new beyond a glimpse of his working style.
transcription_corrections: Top annotations likely read 'We know [by assumption] there exist homotopies'; the second superscript word is illegible.
In the crossed-out disjoint-union diagram the target is likely '(Y⊗I) ⊔ Y'' rather than '(Y⊗I)⊔φ̄', though uncertain.
The interval appears handwritten as 'J' (X⊗J), transcribed as I.
The left-margin label on j likely reads 'non trivial cofibration' (underlined), not 'trivial cofibration'.
'We rewrite the problem, [?] X'⊗I by the arrow h'∘(i⊗I) = v': the inserted word may be 'short-cutting' or 'substituting'.
'whose prism is not commutative' reads more like 'which as prism is not commutative'.
